summary: Observations of radar echoes on scope: lack of information.
description: On December 17, 1957, four military personnel at the Cognac airbase observed a radar echo at 3:01 PM UTC of an object moving from 40 km away and disappearing at 16 km within the fixed radar echoes. The total observation time on radar was 30 seconds, corresponding to a speed of 2,880 km/h. Later that same day, at 3:45 PM UTC, another radar echo was observed at 37 km and disappeared at 25 km. The total observation time was 15 seconds, also corresponding to a speed of 2,880 km/h. An illustrated report with sketches was drawn up by two witnesses. GEIPAN classified this case as Category C due to a lack of information (no visual observation).

summary: Multiple observations of luminous phenomena in the Ardennes sky: lack of information.
description: Between 11:30 PM on October 30, 1957, and 1:30 AM on October 31, 1957, two distinct phenomena were observed by several groups of witnesses in the Ardennes (08). The first group observed, from Louvergny at 11:40 PM, a large-diameter red disk, stationary and facing west, which appeared to split into two parts at 11:50 PM before disappearing. Astronomical verification placed the Moon at an azimuth of 245° and an elevation of 30°, appearing as a tilted semi-disk. The descriptions given did not correspond well with the Moon (elevation and shape). On the same day, a second group on the RN46 between Pauvres and Mazagran observed a small object with green reflections moving rapidly, approximately from southeast to northwest. The observation lasted a few tens of seconds. The witnesses' description suggested the passage of a bolide (meteorite impact). That same evening, a third group, located 100 meters from the Novy-Chevrières level crossing, observed a bright red object in the overcast sky at 11:50 PM, in the direction of the village (see map). No noise was heard during the observation. Despite uncertainties regarding the directions of observation, it is possible that these witnesses mistook the Moon, which was located precisely in that direction (clouds in front of the Moon could have moved). However, this hypothesis is not very compatible with the object's movement as reported by the witnesses. Also on October 30th at 11:50 PM in Ambly-Fleury, a fourth group observed a red glow in the sky in the same direction as the third group. This could also have been a temporary sighting of the Moon through a break in the clouds. Geipan classifies these cases in C due to lack of information and cross-checking: it could be a misinterpretation of the Moon and a passage of a bolide but the elements are not precise enough to confirm these hypotheses.

summary: Flight observations of the SW to NE passage of a luminous object with a trail: probable passage of a meteoroid.
description: On January 3, 1957, at 8:22 PM UTC, three witnesses flying south of Marengo (now Hadjout, Algeria) observed a luminous object with a green, then red, trail crossing the sky for 15 seconds, following a regular downward trajectory from southwest to northeast. Only one witness account was recorded. GEIPAN classified this case as B: probable passage of a meteoroid.
